conventions.Gudi Padwa / Ugadi: Chaitra Shukla Pratipada at sunrise, greater-overlap fallback (drik: same tithi, with 'smarter lunar calendar' fallback for no-sunrise years)
conventions.Rama Navami: Chaitra Shukla Navami at Madhyahna (drik: Madhyahna vyapini)
conventions.Akshaya Tritiya: Vaishakha Shukla Tritiya at Madhyahna (drik: Madhyahna vyapini)
conventions.Raksha Bandhan: Shravana Purnima (nija Shravana) at Aparahna, excluding the Vishti (Bhadra) karana, with a documented fallback when Bhadra covers all of the Purnima-Aparahna time (rule: RakshaBandhanRule). drik's headline date follows its own vyapti logic and can differ by one day (see known_divergences).
conventions.Diwali: Ashwina Amavasya at Pradosh (drik: Lakshmi Puja during Pradosh Kaal; 2026 marked on Chaturdashi because Amavasya begins 11:27 that day)
conventions.Ganesha Chaturthi: Bhadrapada Shukla Chaturthi at Madhyahna (drik: Madhyahna vyapini)
conventions.Krishna Janmashtami: Shravana Krishna Ashtami during Nishita of the night beginning the festival day (drik: Smarta Sampradaya date; Nishita puja may fall past midnight)
conventions.Maha Shivaratri: Magha Krishna Chaturdashi during Nishita of the night beginning the festival day (drik: same)

metadata.city_note: Dates were fetched from the drikpanchang New Delhi pages for each year (2023-2027). drikpanchang lists the same festival DATE for Indian cities (Ahmedabad included); the per-city pages differ only in muhurta times. Ahmedabad was not separately fetched for every festival/year - flagged here rather than assumed silently.

known_divergences.explanation: HYPOTHESIS, UNVERIFIED (drik does not state its date rule): the page facts show Tritiya covers the May 8 Madhyahna too, yet drik lists May 9 — the day with Tritiya at sunrise (their puja runs sunrise to tithi end 09:03). The engine's greater-Madhyahna-overlap rule resolves May 8. Proposed reason: drik prefers the day with the tithi at sunrise for this festival.
known_divergences.drik_page_facts: VERIFIED from the drik page: 'Tritiya Tithi Begins - 11:42 AM on May 08, 2027', 'Tritiya Tithi Ends - 09:03 AM on May 09, 2027'; puja muhurat 05:35 AM to 09:03 AM on May 9 (sunrise to tithi end).

known_divergences.explanation: HYPOTHESIS, UNVERIFIED (drik does not state its date rule): Amavasya spans both Pradosh windows (began during Oct 31). Both days qualify; drik selects Nov 1 (Amavasya-dominant day plus Sthir Lagna criteria), the engine picks the greater Pradosh overlap (Oct 31).

HYPOTHESIS, UNVERIFIED (drik does not state why this midnight): the page facts show the Ashtami spans BOTH midnights (Aug 25 and Aug 26) and drik's Nishita puja for the Aug 25 festival is the night of Aug 25→26 (00:01–00:45 Aug 26). The engine's greater-overlap rule resolves Aug 24, whose night window (Aug 24→25) also has full Ashtami coverage (Ashtami from 20:24 Aug 24). Proposed reason: drik attributes the festival to the day whose second midnight Nishita carries the tithi.
known_divergences.drik_page_facts: VERIFIED from the drik page: 'Ashtami Tithi Begins - 08:24 PM on Aug 24, 2027', 'Ashtami Tithi Ends - 07:19 PM on Aug 25, 2027', 'Nishita Puja Time - 12:01 AM to 12:45 AM, Aug 26'.

known_divergences.explanation: HYPOTHESIS, UNVERIFIED (drik does not state its date rule): Bhadra (Vishti karana) covers the Purnima Aparahna on Aug 8; drik moves to the sunrise-Purnima day (Aug 9), the rule's documented fallback keeps the Purnima-Aparahna day (Aug 8).
HYPOTHESIS, UNVERIFIED (drik does not state its date rule): Purnima begins during the Aug 27 Aparahna; the rule scores that partial Aparahna overlap while drik takes the sunrise-Purnima day (Aug 28).
HYPOTHESIS, UNVERIFIED (drik does not state its date rule): Same pattern as 2026: Purnima begins during the Aug 16 Aparahna; drik takes the sunrise-Purnima day (Aug 17).
